transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-21
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Marcus (SE), Priya (CSM) — Elena, Tomás, Maya, Oliver (Cinderation)

Summary: quick QBR/check-in. Talked about a sudden cost jump in October, two latency blips around 11/4 and 11/12, and a plan to pilot dedicated capacity + KV cache tuning in Dec. Next steps: send cost CSV, run pilot, security docs.

00:00:04 Avery: ok hi everyone thanks for making the time, this is the Q4 health rhythm for Cinderation, just a quick check-in to cover usage, cost, reliability and roadmap alignment
00:00:14 Elena: thanks, yeah we had some fallout last month, saw cost go up, wanted to share context and hear Redwood's recommendations
00:00:21 Marcus: morning all, i'll jump into the latency notes and the pilot ideas — quick note, apologies in advance if my audio pops, new headset
00:00:28 Tomás: no worries, we got one intro Qs: is the spike purely tokens or also embedding-ish usage?
00:00:36 Avery: great question. quick preview — it's token generation primarily; long-form summarization job volume doubled in October during our marketing campaign, also a higher avg seq length which amplified cost
00:00:49 Oliver: from FinOps side we saw a 38% month-over-month increase in hosted invoice line items for 'generation' and curious if there are immediate rightsizing levers
00:00:58 Marcus: yes, levers: batching, prefix caching, quantization profiles, and possibly moving some heavy workloads to Dedicated for predictable throughput. we can show a cost/latency trade-off curve
00:01:12 Elena: we tried auto-batching but saw tail latency spikes, which caused some user complaints. that's what prompted the reliability concern
00:01:20 Priya: maybe helpful to call out the two incidents, maya can you summarize?
00:01:25 Maya: sure — 11/04 at 10:47am PST we had a 350ms increase to p95 on the summarization route for about 7 minutes. then 11/12 had a 600ms spike for 4 minutes during a traffic burst. both coincide with longer than usual contexts
00:01:42 Marcus: quick thought — those sound like KV cache misses plus a bad batching window; if the KV cache gets regenerated or the prefix isn't present, you pay a penalty per token. we often see that when a new model version rolls through or when seq lengths exceed 2048 and kernel selection changes
00:01:59 Tomás: are we seeing model variant fallbacks? we did pin a v1.3 last month but had a canary at v1.4 running for a subset of traffic
00:02:06 Marcus: good catch, we have logs that show ~8% of traffic routed to a fallback variant during the 11/04 window; that would increase latency and token counts
00:02:14 Elena: hmm ok so there's both routing and cache issues, sounds like a multi-factor problem
00:02:21 Avery: to be explicit, we recommend a short December pilot: dedicate a small pool (2 GPUs) and run your heaviest summarization jobs for a 48-hour baseline to compare cost/latency vs hosted. the pilot will include KV cache tuning and a controlled batching policy
00:02:39 Oliver: that sounds reasonable but procurement needs clear numbers. can you give a ballpark delta vs hosted?
00:02:45 Marcus: ballpark — for sustained heavy traffic, Dedicated can reduce per-token cost by ~25-40% depending on utilization and batch efficiency; latency p95 also typically improves 20-45% when KV cache hit rate is high
00:02:59 Oliver: okay we'll need the model assumptions and the GPU SKU called out for procurement
00:03:06 Avery: yes we'll include an annotated cost model and the GPU SKU (A100/RTX depending on region) in the follow-up docs
00:03:13 Priya: quick note on security questions that came up last week — Elena asked about audit logs, SSO, and where inference logs live
00:03:21 Elena: yes SOC2 evidence, SSO through Okta, and how much of the logs are retained in Redwood vs pushed to us
00:03:28 Avery: short answer: we provide audit logs and can integrate with your SIEM via a push; retention levels are configurable — we'll attach the SOC2 snapshot and our logging retention matrix after this call
00:03:40 Tomás: and encryption/KMS — is customer-managed KMS an option for Private/Dedicated?
00:03:46 Marcus: yes, for Private deployments we support customer KMS/HSM integration; for Redwood Dedicated we offer a bring-your-own-key option in certain plans, we'll detail that in the security doc
00:03:58 Maya: perfect, that's one of our procurement blockers so good to see it's supported
00:04:04 Elena: can we also do a short performance run against our longest documents to see where the sequence length cliff happens? we'd like a guardrail for seq length
00:04:13 Marcus: absolutely, we'll run a sequence-length sweep in the pilot and produce a kernel-selection graph — that should show the cliff where memory or kernel path changes cause latency to jump
00:04:24 Oliver: on billing — any chance of a dedicated committed discount for the pilot if we convert? procurement would like to understand minimum commitments
00:04:31 Avery: pilots are typically free for a short baseline, but if you convert to Dedicated we can discuss committed tiers; i'll include a few commitment options and break-even points in the cost model
00:04:42 Tomás: great. also curious about runtime tuning — any quick wins we can try in hosted to reduce cost before the pilot?
00:04:49 Marcus: yes, quick wins: reduce max tokens for summaries where acceptable, enable prefix caching for repeated prompts, add a lightweight client-side cache for certain templates, and lower temperature/penalty settings if you can tolerate slightly more deterministic output for a subset of calls
00:05:05 Elena: we'll try a few of those immediate changes this week, maya and I will coordinate on which routes to change
00:05:12 Priya: i'll put together a short triage checklist so changes are auditable and reversible
00:05:18 Maya: one small point — our infra team wants to know about failover behavior, like model fallback, region fallback; if Dedicated goes down how will routing behave?
00:05:27 Marcus: Redwood's smart routing will fallback to a compatible hosted variant by policy; we can set an automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant or a higher-latency redundant region depending on your SLOs. we'll show config examples in the runbook
00:05:42 Tomás: okay so the plan sounds: short term changes in hosted, then Dec pilot for dedicated + KV tuning, then procurement decision. what's the measurement plan?
00:05:52 Avery: measurement plan — baseline p50/p95 latency, tokens/req, cost per 1M tokens, KV hit rate, and error rate. we'll instrument synthetic and a small sample of live traffic with shadowing to avoid impacting users
00:06:07 Elena: how long for pilot data to be meaningful? 48-72 hours for baseline, but longer if you want traffic seasonality represented
00:06:14 Marcus: 48 hours is fine to see kernel/cliff effects; for cost smoothing i'd recommend a week but we can start with 48-hour intensive run
00:06:23 Oliver: procurement timeline: assuming we like pilot, we'd need a PO in mid-Jan. is that feasible?
00:06:30 Avery: yes that's feasible, procurement and legal timeline looks like mid-Jan PO can be done if pilot approves
00:06:36 Tomás: any blockers on our side to start pilot?
00:06:39 Marcus: we'll need network allowlist entries for the pilot endpoints and team contacts for playbook coordination. also a short test dataset for the sequence sweep
00:06:50 Maya: we can provide the dataset and allowlist today, i'll upload to the shared drive after this call
00:06:57 Priya: noted, i'll send the pilot checklist and schedule a 2-hour kickoff next Tuesday (11/30) pending calendars
00:07:04 Elena: sounds good — real quick, two process questions: 1) what happens if we hit a regression in quality after quantization? and 2) how do we track quality delta?
00:07:15 Marcus: we run evals on a holdout prompt set pre/post quantization; if regression exceeds your threshold we'll fallback to higher-precision variant automatically. Redwood Optimize has a quality monitor and we can attach regression alerts to a prompt set
00:07:29 Tomás: ok that helps. on the security side, Oliver wants a short SOC2 packet and an SLA excerpt
00:07:35 Avery: yes we'll attach SOC2 summary, SOC2 cert link, and the SLA excerpt in the follow-up email
00:07:41 Oliver: thanks, that will unblock procurement review
00:07:44 Elena: one more ask — can we get a replay of the exact traffic that tripped 11/12? we'd like to run it locally against our safeguards
00:07:53 Marcus: we can provide a scrubbed replay and the request IDs; however some PII considerations mean you might get an anonymized sample. we'll coordinate with your security team
00:08:04 Maya: that's fine as long as the sequence length and prompt templates are preserved
00:08:09 Avery: ok recap: Redwood action items are cost CSV + annotated model assumptions (Avery), pilot runbook + baseline harness and replay sample (Marcus), SOC2 + SLA excerpt (Priya). Customer action items: provide peak windows and dataset, confirm pilot KPIs, procurement contact info (Elena/Oliver)
00:08:30 Tomás: perfect, can we lock in the kickoff time now? you said next Tue (11/30) — mornings are best for us
00:08:36 Priya: i'll propose 9:00am PST and include a Doodle if that doesn't work
00:08:41 Elena: 9 works for me, maya confirmed too
00:08:45 Oliver: procurement will be on the invite for the kickoff as optional
00:08:49 Avery: excellent. any other items before we wrap?
00:08:54 Maya: just to note — we'll monitor Sentry for user-facing errors during the pilot; i'll share alert thresholds
00:09:00 Marcus: i'll put together a short doc on KV cache tuning heuristics and batching window suggestions
00:09:07 Tomás: thanks everyone, appreciate the pragmatic plan
00:09:11 Avery: thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts by EOD Friday. end of notes.

(there is some minor transcription noise beyond this point, a brief crosstalk and hold music while scheduling an invite)

57:00:12 Speaker 1: yeah okay cool see you next week
57:00:20 Speaker 2: bye
57:00:35 End of recording
